title: Choose the look of the new MARCUS
question: Pick the design direction for the new MARCUS (landing page and curation tool). You can also ask for a fresh set, safer or bolder.

options.label: The Loupe
options.lineage: the hexagonal lens in the MARCUS logo, made into the one optical instrument of the whole interface
options.thesis: A green hexagonal lens moves over real paper pages, and whatever it passes turns into a recognised, checkable structure.
options.viewport: Landing: a full-height navy desk with one real page at large scale; the lens sweeps across it and each drawing it crosses lifts out as a structure with its SMILES; headline and Start button sit left. Tool: focus mode shows the crop inside the lens, its page around it.
options.risk: Built on the logo's own idea, so it can read obvious if the lens is just decoration instead of the real review instrument.

raised.raise: Review is one unbroken row of toggle keys per page with a running cursor; A/R arm a structure like stepping a pattern.
A failure never disappears: a failed page stays in place as a stalled sheet with its reason printed on it.
Light is state: accepted structures are lit, unreviewed ones wait unlit, rejected ones fold flat.

options.label: Atom Colours
options.lineage: the CPK atom colour convention every chemist reads at a glance (carbon black, nitrogen blue, oxygen red, sulfur yellow)
options.thesis: The whole interface is coloured like a molecule model: big fields of nitrogen blue and oxygen red, carbon-black type, with the logo's green as the 'accepted' colour.
options.viewport: Landing: a split field, nitrogen-blue left with the headline in white, a large structure drawn in CPK colours right; engines shown as atom-coloured tiles. Tool: white workspace, colour only on states and engine tags.
options.risk: Familiar to chemists and strong, but red means oxygen here, so error states need another signal (shape and icon, not only red).

options.label: Curation Ledger
options.lineage: Japanese high-density web pages: tiny type, ruled boxed modules, one utility accent
options.thesis: Everything a curator needs on one screen: a dense ruled mosaic of structure modules, each with a small green tab, nothing wasted.
options.viewport: Tool-first: the paper's structures as a tight grid of ruled modules with SMILES, engine and state visible at once; landing is a dense one-screen overview.
options.case: Fuses well for power curators (hundreds of structures per screen); weaker for first-time visitors who need one clear story.
options.risk: Can feel cramped and unfriendly to students trying one paper.

options.label: Rhythm machine step row
options.thesis: Review as a sequencer: structures as step keys under a chase light.
options.viewport: A row of sixteen keys per page.
options.case: Chemists do not identify with music hardware; the metaphor hides the structures.
options.kept: One unbroken review row with keyboard-armed states.

options.label: Depot destination blind
options.thesis: Status as cloth courses stepping under a window.
options.case: Strong status grammar, but no link to chemistry or papers.
options.kept: A fault is a visible stalled state, never an absence.

options.label: Akari light sculpture
options.thesis: Results as lit paper volumes in a dim room.
options.case: Calm and beautiful, but too soft for a bold modern tool.
options.kept: Light as state: lit means accepted.

options.label: Kinetic sand glyphs
options.thesis: Commands as rings of glyphs in raised sand.
options.case: No link to the curator's task; radial controls slow review.
options.kept: One central focus with everything else in rings around it (focus mode).
options.risk: Hard to use for list work.

options.label: Alphabet storm
options.thesis: Letters condense into words and weather.
options.kept: Type as material: the MARCUS wordmark at monumental scale.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean science-tool website: white pages, navy text, green accent, a molecule picture up top, done very well.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and Start button left, a screenshot of the tool right; three feature blocks below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like many other science tools by design.
